assessmentSummary.identity: One unloaded side-lying open-and-return repetition. Start with hips and knees comfortably bent and stacked, both straight arms stacked at shoulder height in front, and the pelvis comparatively stable. Move the top arm in a controlled arc as the rib cage and trunk rotate open, stop at comfortable controllable range without requiring the hand to touch the floor, then return along the declared path until the hands stack. One return to the stacked-hands start is one repetition. Perform and record each side separately. Range, pace, dose, brief end hold, eye-follow or supported-neutral-head strategy, and stable comfort props are delivery annotations. A different leg base, mandatory overhead windmill path, bent-arm rib pull, manual force, resistance, wall base, or assessment protocol changes the task.
currentCardFindings: Source 28 has one skeletal baseline variant, two incomplete legacy profiles, empty controlled taxonomy/anatomy/load/fatigue/constraints/support data, zero calibration, no canonical evidence or alternates, and four unreviewed general media links.

Active Open Book Rotation and archived Open Book T-Spine Rotation definitions describe the same side-lying, knees-stacked, top-arm-open, upper-trunk-rotation, slow-return identity and should consolidate into Source 28 while preserving legacy aliases and lineage.
Legacy age minima and published flags are unsupported exercise-card classification or approval claims and must be cleared.
assessmentSummary.programmingDecision: Select only for a low-load side-lying open-and-return rotation when floor access, side-lying tolerance, shoulder and spinal range, knee stacking, dose, and downstream budgets fit. Range, pace, repetitions, sets, rest, brief hold, gaze strategy, and stable comfort props are delivery annotations. Use Thread-the-Needle for quadruped arm-driven rotation or separately authored cards when the base, leg configuration, arm path, external force, assessment purpose, or movement sequence changes.

currentCardSnapshot.description: Lie on one side with hips and knees comfortably bent and stacked, both straight arms stacked at shoulder height in front, and the pelvis comparatively stable. Move the top arm in a controlled arc while the rib cage and trunk rotate open. Stop at comfortable controllable range without requiring the hand to touch the floor, then return along the declared path until the hands stack. That return is one repetition. Perform and record each side separately. Range, pace, dose, brief end hold, gaze strategy, and stable comfort props are delivery annotations. A different leg base, mandatory windmill path, bent-arm rib pull, manual force, external resistance, wall base, or assessment protocol is another task.

evidence.sourceTitle: Physiotherapy exercises for breast pain with chest wall musculoskeletal symptoms
claims: Leeds specifies side lying with bent knees together, both straight arms stacked in front, the upper arm moving in an arc behind the body, the eyes following the hand, the knees remaining together on the floor, and a slow return.

Model active thoracolumbar axial rotation with rib-cage rotation and top-shoulder horizontal abduction or transverse extension while the pelvis and stacked legs provide a comparatively stable base; do not claim isolated thoracic motion or quantified muscle force.

evidence.sourceTitle: Physiotherapy exercises for breast pain with chest wall musculoskeletal symptoms
claims: The task requires one side-lying setup, stacked lower-body support, a controlled top-arm arc, trunk rotation, a same-path return, and completion on both sides with low external load.
No source assigns a Vortex score or participant classification; exercise complexity 22 and physical difficulty 10 are review-only proposals, and overall difficulty is their maximum.
The exact task is an unloaded side-lying rotation under body-segment mass with one arm moving and the lower body remaining supported; no required external implement is described.

Track side, complete repetitions, arm path, rotation range, knee and pelvic stability, head strategy, duration, symptoms, and same-session shoulder and spinal-range exposure; no source quantifies tissue force or proves one universal fatigue or recovery interval.

evidence.sourceTitle: Interventions for the Management of Acute and Chronic Low Back Pain: Revision 2021
evidence.sourcePublisher: Journal of Orthopaedic & Sports Physical Therapy / Academy of Orthopaedic Physical Therapy
claims: The low-back-pain guideline supports individualized exercise in applicable contexts while emphasizing patient-centered assessment and red-flag screening rather than universal assignment.

Selection requires safe floor transfer, side-lying tolerance, comfortable controllable trunk and shoulder motion, symptom reporting, and exit; conflicting trauma, neurologic symptoms, clinical restrictions, support intolerance, or transfer limits require another card or escalation without diagnosis.

evidence.sourceTitle: Interventions for the Management of Acute and Chronic Low Back Pain: Revision 2021
evidence.sourcePublisher: Journal of Orthopaedic & Sports Physical Therapy / Academy of Orthopaedic Physical Therapy
claims: Clinical guidance distinguishes general exercise from evaluation of serious pathology and neurologic deficit and does not make one rotation drill universally appropriate.

Stop for sharp, increasing, radiating, or unfamiliar pain; numbness, tingling, weakness, saddle sensory change, bowel or bladder change, dizziness, faintness, support loss, inability to preserve the declared task, or participant request.
Dynamic Health presents Open Book as a controlled mid-back mobility exercise performed on both sides, not as a strength, load, diagnosis, or readiness test.

Use conservative contextual doses, count only complete hand-stack to open range to hand-stack repetitions, and revalidate cumulative active spinal range, shoulder arc, floor-work, duration, and downstream loading budgets.

evidence.sourceTitle: Physiotherapy exercises for breast pain with chest wall musculoskeletal symptoms
claims: The direct side-lying setup, arm arc, eye-follow option, knees-together constraint, slow return, and five-per-side example can be translated into concise athlete instructions.

Athlete support must explain one complete counted repetition, preserve stacked knees and a stable pelvis, permit a neutral supported head when gaze following is not appropriate, avoid forcing the hand to the floor, and state symptom stops.
Dynamic Health gives a simple side-lying, knees-bent, hands-together setup and a top-arm-to-ceiling then chest-opening sequence completed on both sides.

Provide front and overhead demonstration, a written start-open-return sequence, named working side, optional stable head or knee support, smaller range, fewer repetitions, slower pace, and rest; separately author support-changing or non-floor tasks.
Five exact-title YouTube candidates returned current oEmbed title, channel, thumbnail, and iframe metadata on 2026-08-09.

oEmbed health does not prove playback, exact setup or repetition boundary, range, captions, accessibility, cue quality, safety, conflicts, reviewer identity, card-version match, or approval; all five remain candidates.

evidence.sourceTitle: Physiotherapy exercises for breast pain with chest wall musculoskeletal symptoms
claims: Leeds directly names Open Book and specifies side lying, stacked forward arms, an upper-arm arc behind the body, knees together on the floor, and a slow return, supporting one open-and-return repetition boundary.
Vortex consolidates the orthographic Open Book duplicates and keeps one standard long-arm, bent-stacked-knee exact variant; range, dose, gaze strategy, and stable comfort props remain annotations.
The task is an unloaded side-lying trunk-rotation and top-arm-reaching action with the legs providing a stable base and work completed on both sides.
Use controlled rotate and reach patterns; mobility is purpose rather than an invented movement-pattern key.

evidence.sourceTitle: Reliability and exploration of the side-lying thoraco-lumbar rotation measurement
evidence.sourcePublisher: North American Journal of Sports Physical Therapy
claims: The measurement study reports that thoracic rotation is difficult to isolate clinically and therefore measures global thoracolumbar rotation in side lying.
Do not promise isolated thoracic motion, prescribe a universal normal angle, or infer clinical benefit from measurement reliability.

evidence.sourceTitle: Physiotherapy exercises for breast pain with chest wall musculoskeletal symptoms
claims: Leeds gives five repetitions on each side as one contextual example and directs a slow return.
Author a conservative review-only range of one to two sets and three to six complete repetitions per side; calculate actual time and stop before position or motion control degrades.
Dynamic Health supports knees bent, hands stacked forward, top arm reaching to the ceiling, chest opening to the other side, head following the arm, slow return, and completion on both sides.

The card counts the return to stacked hands, keeps the knees together and pelvis comparatively stable, permits supported neutral head position when required, and never requires floor contact at end range.

evidence.sourceTitle: Interventions for the Management of Acute and Chronic Low Back Pain: Revision 2021
evidence.sourcePublisher: Journal of Orthopaedic & Sports Physical Therapy / Academy of Orthopaedic Physical Therapy
claims: Clinical guidance supports individualized exercise and monitoring with red-flag screening rather than universal exercise assignment.

Coach support must verify floor transfer, side-lying and shoulder tolerance, exact setup, knee and pelvic stability, top-arm path, comfortable range, first fault, actual dose, symptoms, and escalation without diagnosis.

evidence.sourceTitle: Clinical reasoning framework for thoracic spine exercise prescription in sport: a systematic review and narrative synthesis
claims: The thoracic exercise review distinguishes exercises by plane, base, and task intent, so side-lying rotation should not be treated as equivalent to quadruped, kneeling, loaded, or multi-planar tasks.

Keep windmills, rib pulls, split-leg anchors, assessments, wall bases, quadruped rotations, manual assistance, resistance, and combined stretches outside the single exact standard variant until separately authored and reviewed.

alternateAssessments.name: Open Book Rotation, Open Book T-Spine Rotation, or Side-Lying Thoracic Rotation
alternateAssessments.rationale: These titles retain the bent-stacked-knee side-lying start, stacked forward arms, top-arm opening with trunk rotation, and controlled return.

alternateAssessments.name: Stacked-Knee Long-Arm Open-and-Return
alternateAssessments.rationale: This is the one authored exact variant when the side-lying base, stacked knees, long top-arm opening path, trunk rotation, and hand-restack repetition boundary remain exact.

alternateAssessments.name: Left or Right Side
alternateAssessments.rationale: The working side changes laterality and must be recorded, but the exact movement identity is unchanged.

alternateAssessments.name: Smaller or Larger Comfortable Opening Range
alternateAssessments.rationale: Range remains a delivery setting when the same setup, path, lower-body stability, and return boundary remain observable.

alternateAssessments.name: Open Book Tempo, Repetitions, Sets, Rest, or Brief End Hold
alternateAssessments.rationale: Pace, volume, rest, and a non-forced pause change dose rather than the movement identity.

alternateAssessments.name: Eyes Follow Hand or Supported Neutral Head
alternateAssessments.rationale: Head and gaze strategy may be adjusted for comfort when the trunk and arm task remains exact and cervical motion is recorded.

alternateAssessments.name: Optional Mat, Head Towel, or Small Knee Comfort Support
alternateAssessments.rationale: Stable comfort support is an annotation only when it does not alter the stacked-knee base, arm path, trunk action, or endpoint.

alternateAssessments.name: Side-Lying Windmill
alternateAssessments.rationale: A mandatory large overhead circular arm path adds shoulder flexion, abduction, circumduction, space, and distinct completion rules.

alternateAssessments.name: Bent-Elbow Rib Pull
alternateAssessments.rationale: Grasping the ribs or placing the hand behind the head removes the long-arm book-opening path and may add self-assistance or different leverage.

alternateAssessments.name: Split-Leg Top-Knee-Anchored Open Book
alternateAssessments.rationale: A straight bottom leg with the top hip and knee flexed onto the floor or a bolster materially changes pelvic support, hip position, equipment, and observable compensation.

alternateAssessments.name: Foam-Roller-Supported Top-Knee Open Book
alternateAssessments.rationale: Supporting the top knee forward on a roller changes leg geometry, equipment, pelvic constraint, station setup, and exit beyond a small comfort prop.

alternateAssessments.name: Wall Open Book
alternateAssessments.rationale: Standing or half-kneeling against a wall changes base, balance, gravity, support, floor-transfer requirements, and arm path.

alternateAssessments.name: Quadruped Thread-the-Needle
alternateAssessments.rationale: Quadruped support and an arm threading under or opening from the body change contacts, load, path, and repetition boundaries.

alternateAssessments.name: Quadruped Spinal Circles
alternateAssessments.rationale: A fixed-contact global multi-planar spinal circle uses a different support base, action sequence, directions, and counted checkpoint.

alternateAssessments.name: Cat-Cow
alternateAssessments.rationale: Cat-Cow is a quadruped sagittal flexion-extension cycle rather than side-lying axial rotation with a moving top arm.

alternateAssessments.name: Supine Lower-Trunk Rotation or Lumbar Twist
alternateAssessments.rationale: Supine bilateral leg rotation changes the moving segments, limb driver, pelvis action, support, and endpoint.

alternateAssessments.name: Bretzel or Combined Side-Lying Hip-and-Shoulder Stretch
alternateAssessments.rationale: A combined stretch adds leg grasp, hip extension or knee flexion, shoulder position, passive force, consent, and distinct stops.

alternateAssessments.name: Side-Lying Thoracolumbar Rotation Measurement
alternateAssessments.rationale: A measured assessment uses standardized positioning, an inclinometer or landmark, examiner procedure, and a measurement outcome rather than exercise repetitions.

alternateAssessments.name: Banded or Cable-Resisted Open Book
alternateAssessments.rationale: An anchor and external resistance add force direction, load magnitude, equipment, fatigue, failure, and setup requirements.

alternateAssessments.name: Partner- or Clinician-Assisted Open Book
alternateAssessments.rationale: Manual force introduces consent, contact, force dosing, clinical scope, monitoring, and different stop rules.
